o: We maintain orders keyed by id, each with a type and price, supporting add, modify price, cancel, and listing all active ids sharing a type and price. With at most 2000 calls, almost anything works, but hash maps give O(1) average per operation. In the example, orders 1 and 2 sit at (buy,1); modifying order 1 moves it to price 3, so only order 2 remains at (buy,1), and cancellations empty the group.
k: Keep a map id -> (type, price) plus a map (type, price) -> set of ids; every mutation updates both structures.
Using a set (or TreeSet) per group makes listing trivial and removals O(1) average.

a.i: The primary map answers existence and lets modify/cancel find the old group key; the group map collects ids per (type, price) bucket. Modify = remove from old bucket, insert into new. Cancel = remove from bucket and primary map.
s: addOrder: store attributes, add id to bucket.
modifyOrder: move id between buckets, update price.
getOrdersAtPrice: return a copy of the bucket (possibly empty).
a.t: O(1) average per add/modify/cancel, O(size of group) per query

w: Straightforward design problem; the only real decision is the bucket key (concatenate type and price, or encode as a long). Pitfall: forgetting to remove the id from its OLD price bucket on modify, which causes ghost entries. Follow-up: return ids in insertion order (use LinkedHashSet / OrderedDict), or support matching best buy/sell (use heaps or TreeSets per side).
